Tersus GNSS AG993: Modular autosteer kit with built-in satellite correction fallback

 02-07 | Autonomous/semi-autosteering systems | News

LinkedInFacebookXWhatsAppPrint

Core components include the GC30 Guidance Controller, TC120 tablet terminal, TES30 electric steering motor, steering wheel, main cable, camera, power switch mount and vehicle-specific brackets and spline accessories. Photos: Tersus GNSS

Tersus GNSS has brought the AG993 to market – a modular automatic steering retrofit system that combines high-precision GNSS positioning with the company’s own TAP satellite-based correction service and conventional RTK support. The AG993 has now been added to the Future Farming Autosteer Retrofit Kits Catalogue.

The system is designed to deliver better than 2.5 cm autosteering accuracy, with a working speed range of 0.2 to 30 km/h and support for ultra-low-speed operation from as slow as 0.1 km/h. Automatic U-turns on headlands are included as standard.

A defining feature is the TAP service – Tersus Advanced Positioning – which delivers real-time correction via L-band satellite signal rather than depending on a local base station or mobile network.

In areas where cellular coverage is unreliable or RTK infrastructure is absent, TAP allows the AG993 to maintain centimetre-level accuracy independently. If regular RTK correction is temporarily lost, the TAPFill function switches to TAP as a backup source automatically, keeping the positioning result aligned with the RTK coordinate reference frame to maintain guidance consistency.

If GNSS signals are lost entirely, or positioning quality drops below the required threshold, the software issues a status warning and the operator must disengage autosteer, check the equipment and signal conditions, and resume only when conditions are confirmed suitable.

Tersus states that the AG993 is compatible with over 90% of agricultural vehicles across various brands, requiring a suitable steering column position, power supply, mounting space for the controller and tablet, and a clear location for GNSS reception.Modular installation, broad compatibility

Core components include the GC30 Guidance Controller, TC120 tablet terminal, TES30 electric steering motor, steering wheel, main cable, camera, power switch mount and vehicle-specific brackets and spline accessories. Thanks to its modular design, installation is relatively straightforward, followed by vehicle calibration in the TersusAG software. Tersus recommends installation by trained personnel or an authorised dealer.

Tersus states that the AG993 is compatible with over 90% of agricultural vehicles across various brands, requiring a suitable steering column position, power supply, mounting space for the controller and tablet, and a clear location for GNSS reception.

The core system can in principle be moved to another compatible vehicle, though brackets, spline type, vehicle parameters and calibration would all need to be checked and adjusted, and a full reinstallation and recalibration would be required.

The AG993 supports all major satellite constellations – GPS, GLONASS, BeiDou (including BDS-3), Galileo, QZSS, SBAS and IRNSS – plus the L-band correction signal used for TAP service – Tersus Advanced Positioning.Guidance patterns and software updates

The AG993 supports straight lines, curve lines, boundary curves and four auto-generated smart path types, as well as automatic U-turns within field boundaries. Software and firmware updates are issued on a regular basis, with a major official release planned roughly every six months and smaller maintenance updates potentially issued quarterly. The update schedule is timed around the agricultural calendar to ensure stable versions are available before the spring seeding and autumn harvest seasons. Update costs may vary by market, distributor and service package.

Licensing covers controller registration and optional TAP correction subscriptions, selectable by duration and application. Advanced functions such as Auto U-turn are currently available without an additional unlock, though licensing policy for advanced features may change in future. ISOBUS-related function licenses are also anticipated as that integration develops.

Notably, Tersus is also developing an open-source-oriented integration path designed to work with the AgOpenGPS community, positioning it separately from the standard commercial licensing model. Tersus believes linking the GC30 controller to the AgOpenGPS ecosystem could create a positive feedback loop, with users gaining access to Tersus’s hardware platform, GNSS/INS fusion algorithms and motor-control expertise, while the community contributes more flexible applications and integrations.

The TC120 Android tablet (10.1″/25.7 cm, 1280 × 800 resolution) is rated IP67.Looking ahead: autonomy, sensors and data ecosystems

Mark Chen, Director of Digital Media at Tersus GNSS, sees the AG993 as a foundation for broader developments in agricultural automation. He points to ISOBUS Tractor Implement Management as one key direction: “Forward speed, PTO, hydraulics, hitch position, spray sections, seeding units, application rate and implement status can all affect both operation quality and safety.”

On the sensor side, Chen says that GNSS and autosteer alone will not be sufficient for higher-level systems: “Multi-sensor fusion, environmental understanding and obstacle detection will become core capabilities. Future systems will increasingly combine cameras, LiDAR, radar, ultrasonic sensors, IMU, vehicle CAN data, implement status sensors and AI/edge computing for obstacle recognition, risk assessment, safe stopping, path adjustment, implement-issue detection and remote alerts.” He points to John Deere’s autonomy solutions as examples of where leading systems are already heading.

Data connectivity is another dimension, Chen highlights. “Platforms such as xFarm, MyEasyFarm, NEXT Farming, John Deere Operations Center, FendtONE and agrirouter will influence how agricultural automation data moves between machines, implements, farms and service providers.”

Finally, Chen flags regulatory and cybersecurity requirements as growing factors, particularly in Europe: “As systems move from autosteer toward supervised autonomy, they will need clearer human-machine responsibility boundaries, including geofencing, no-go zones, emergency stop, manual override, remote monitoring, operation logs, diagnostics, software updates, permission management and cybersecurity.”

Specifications and pricing

The AG993 supports all major satellite constellations — GPS, GLONASS, BeiDou (including BDS-3), Galileo, QZSS, SBAS and IRNSS — plus the L-band correction signal used for TAP. The TC120 Android tablet (10.1″/25.7 cm, 1280 × 800 resolution) and GC30 Guidance Controller are both rated IP67; the TES30 electric motor is rated IP55. A 12-inch (30.5 cm) tablet terminal is also in development. ISOBUS VT&TC compatibility is in development, with section control for sprayers and seed drills expected to follow once ISOBUS/Task Controller integration is complete.

The AG993 carries an indicative retail price from approximately US $4,000 – US $8,000 (€3,509 to €7,018, exchange rate 01-07-2026), subject to the dealer, region, installation and configuration.

translationZh:
Tersus GNSS已将AG993推向市场——这是一套模块化自动转向改装系统，将高精度GNSS定位与公司自有的TAP卫星校正服务及传统RTK支持相结合。AG993现已收录至《Future Farming自动转向改装套件目录》。

该系统旨在提供优于2.5厘米的自动转向精度，工作速度范围为0.2至30公里/小时，并支持低至0.1公里/小时的超低速作业。地头自动掉头功能为标准配置。

其一个显著特点是TAP服务——Tersus高级定位——通过L波段卫星信号提供实时校正，而非依赖本地基站或移动网络。

在蜂窝网络覆盖不可靠或缺少RTK基础设施的地区，TAP使AG993能够独立维持厘米级精度。如果常规RTK校正暂时丢失，TAPFill功能会自动切换到TAP作为备份源，使定位结果与RTK坐标参考框架保持一致，以维持导航一致性。

如果GNSS信号完全丢失，或定位质量降至所需阈值以下，软件会发出状态警告，操作员必须解除自动转向，检查设备和信号状况，仅在确认条件合适后才能恢复作业。

Tersus表示，AG993兼容各品牌超过90%的农用车辆，要求有合适的转向柱位置、电源、控制器和平板电脑的安装空间，以及清晰的GNSS接收位置。

**模块化设计，广泛兼容**

核心组件包括GC30导航控制器、TC120平板终端、TES30电动转向电机、方向盘、主电缆、摄像头、电源开关支架以及针对特定车辆的支架和花键附件。得益于模块化设计，安装相对简单，随后在TersusAG软件中进行车辆校准。Tersus建议由经过培训的人员或授权经销商进行安装。

Tersus表示，AG993兼容各品牌超过90%的农用车辆，要求有合适的转向柱位置、电源、控制器和平板电脑的安装空间，以及清晰的GNSS接收位置。

核心系统原则上可以移至另一辆兼容车辆上，但支架、花键类型、车辆参数和校准都需要检查和调整，并且需要完全重新安装和重新校准。

AG993支持所有主要卫星星座——GPS、GLONASS、北斗（包括BDS-3）、Galileo、QZSS、SBAS和IRNSS——以及用于TAP服务（Tersus高级定位）的L波段校正信号。

**导航模式与软件更新**

AG993支持直线、曲线、边界曲线和四种自动生成的智能路径类型，以及田界内的自动U型转弯。软件和固件定期更新，计划大约每六个月发布一次重大官方版本，并可能每季度发布较小的维护更新。更新时间表围绕农业日历安排，以确保在春季播种和秋季收获季节之前提供稳定版本。更新成本可能因市场、分销商和服务套餐而异。

许可涵盖控制器注册和可选的TAP校正订阅，可按时长和应用选择。自动U型转弯等高级功能目前无需额外解锁即可使用，但高级功能的许可政策未来可能会发生变化。随着ISOBUS集成的发展，预计还将推出与ISOBUS相关的功能许可。

值得注意的是，Tersus还在开发一种面向开源的集成路径，旨在与AgOpenGPS社区协作，将其与标准商业许可模式区分开来。Tersus认为，将GC30控制器与AgOpenGPS生态系统连接起来可以形成正反馈循环，用户可以获得Tersus的硬件平台、GNSS/INS融合算法和电机控制专业知识，而社区则贡献更灵活的应用程序和集成方案。

TC120安卓平板电脑（10.1英寸/25.7厘米，1280×800分辨率）防护等级为IP67。

**展望未来：自主性、传感器与数据生态系统**

Tersus GNSS数字媒体总监Mark Chen将AG993视为更广泛的农业自动化发展的基础。他指出ISOBUS拖拉机农具管理是一个关键方向：“前进速度、PTO、液压系统、悬挂位置、喷药段、播种单元、施用量和农具状态都会影响作业质量和安全性。”

在传感器方面，Chen表示，仅靠GNSS和自动转向不足以支持更高级别的系统：“多传感器融合、环境理解和障碍物检测将成为核心能力。未来的系统将越来越多地结合摄像头、激光雷达、雷达、超声波传感器、IMU、车辆CAN数据、农具状态传感器以及AI/边缘计算，用于障碍物识别、风险评估、安全停车、路径调整、农具问题检测和远程警报。”他提到约翰迪尔的自主解决方案是领先系统的发展方向。

数据连接是另一个维度，Chen强调。“诸如xFarm、MyEasyFarm、NEXT Farming、John Deere Operations Center、FendtONE和agrirouter等平台将影响农业自动化数据如何在机器、农具、农场和服务提供商之间流动。”

最后，Chen指出监管和网络安全要求是日益增长的因素，尤其是在欧洲：“随着系统从自动转向向监督式自主发展，它们将需要更清晰的人机责任边界，包括地理围栏、禁入区、紧急停止、手动覆盖、远程监控、操作日志、诊断、软件更新、权限管理和网络安全。”

**规格与定价**

AG993支持所有主要卫星星座——GPS、GLONASS、北斗（包括BDS-3）、Galileo、QZSS、SBAS和IRNSS——以及用于TAP的L波段校正信号。TC120安卓平板电脑（10.1英寸/25.7厘米，1280×800分辨率）和GC30导航控制器均达到IP67防护等级；TES30电动电机达到IP55防护等级。一款12英寸（30.5厘米）平板终端也在开发中。ISOBUS VT&TC兼容性正在开发中，一旦ISOBUS/任务控制器集成完成，预计将推出针对喷雾机和播种机的段控制功能。

AG993的指示性零售价约为4,000至8,000美元（3,509至7,018欧元，汇率日期2026年1月7日），具体取决于经销商、地区、安装和配置。
